groups.title: Experience and advancement
groups.intro: Experience points and how they are spent; the sources of study: exposure, practice, adventure, training and teaching.

entries.title: Using Experience Points
entries.summary: Explains how experience points raise Arts and Abilities and gives the cost formulas for gaining a level in each.
quotes: INCREASE AN ABILITY BY ONE: (Ability + 1) x 5 experience points
INCREASE AN ART BY ONE: Art + 1 experience points

entries.title: Advancement Tables
entries.summary: Lookup table of the experience points needed to buy a score from zero, or to raise it by one, for Arts and Abilities.
quotes: To buy: The number of experience points required to raise a score from zero to that number.

entries.title: Advancement Total
entries.summary: Defines the Advancement Total earned by a season of study and the rule that only one source of experience may be used per season, apart from Exposure.
quotes: ADVANCEMENT TOTAL: Source Quality + Bonus from Virtues - Penalty from Flaws

entries.title: Calculating Experience Points
entries.summary: Three-step procedure from Source Quality to Advancement Total to experience points gained, and which Virtues and Flaws modify each step.

entries.title: Exposure
entries.summary: The weakest source of experience: simply using or assisting with an Ability or Art during a season; experience may be split between two subjects, and lab work grants Exposure to lead magus and assistants.
quotes: EXPOSURE SOURCE QUALITY: Two

entries.title: Adventure Experience
entries.summary: Adventures give a whole season of experience with a Source Quality set by the storyguide, which can be split among Abilities used and Arts used on stage.
quotes: ADVENTURE SOURCE QUALITY: 5–10

entries.title: Practice
entries.summary: Full-time self-directed study of an Ability, with special higher Source Qualities for native-tongue languages, Area Lore, feedback-rich crafts and practising spells for mastery; Arts cannot be raised this way.
quotes: PRACTICE SOURCE QUALITY: 4–8, usually 4

entries.title: Training
entries.summary: One-on-one instruction by a master who has a higher score and is using the Ability to earn a living; Hermetic Arts cannot be raised by training.
quotes: TRAINING SOURCE QUALITY: Master's score in Ability being taught + 3
TRAINING GAIN LIMIT: Master's score in Ability being taught

entries.title: Teaching
entries.summary: Lessons from a teacher with a higher score and a shared language, with Source Quality depending on the teacher's Communication and Teaching and a bonus that depends on class size; Arts may only be taught one-on-one.
quotes: TEACHING SOURCE QUALITY: Teacher's Communication + Teaching + 3 + bonus
TEACHING GAIN LIMIT: The teacher's score in the Art or Ability

entries.title: Studying From Books
entries.summary: Rules for studying summae and tractatus: language and literacy prerequisites, level limits for summae, one-time study of each tractatus, and Supernatural Abilities needing a score of at least one.
quotes: SUMMAE: Source Quality and Level
SUMMA GAIN LIMIT: Summa Level
TRACTATUS: Source Quality

entries.title: Assigning Seasons
entries.summary: Explains how seasons are abstractly assigned to work and study for ordinary characters, and how magi differ because lab work takes a whole real season and they have genuinely free seasons.

entries.title: Gain Limit
entries.summary: A study source with its own level caps the score a student can reach from it, and gives no experience towards the next level.
quotes: This limit is called the Gain Limit.

entries.title: Vis Study
entries.summary: Magi study an Art from raw vis, consuming pawns of that Art's vis for the season; a double botch on the stress die can lead to Wizard's Twilight.
quotes: VIS SOURCE QUALITY: Stress Die + Aura Bonus

entries.title: Worship
entries.requires: Christian character with access to a chapel or church (similar activities for other Divine faiths)
entries.summary: A free-season devotional routine whose Source Quality is the Divine aura of the church, spent on Church Lore, Concentration, Music or Divine-aligned Abilities and Arts.
quotes: Worship has a Source Quality equal to the Divine aura in the church.

entries.title: Distractions
entries.summary: Distractions of more than a month reduce an Advancement or writing total by a fraction for each full month lost, rounding fractions up.
quotes: For every full month lost, reduce the total by one third of its original amount.

entries.title: Learning Supernatural Abilities
entries.summary: How a character first learns a Supernatural Ability by Training or Teaching, with a Source Quality penalty equal to scores in other Supernatural Abilities and a larger penalty if the Hermetic Arts have been opened.
quotes: SUPERNATURAL ABILITY SOURCE QUALITY: Normal Source Quality - Total Score in Supernatural Abilities

groups.title: Books and reading
groups.intro: Summae and tractatus: their Level and Quality, reading them, and how they are written and copied.

entries.title: Writing Books
entries.summary: Prerequisite scores for writing a useful book and the Source Quality formulas for summae and tractatus.
quotes: SUMMA SOURCE QUALITY: Author's Communication + 6 + bonus
Tractatus Source Quality: Author's Communication + 6

entries.title: Writing Summae
entries.summary: How a summa's Level and Quality are chosen, the Quality bonus for a lower Level, and how many points per season accumulate until the book is finished, with a worked example.
quotes: the summa is complete.

entries.title: Writing Tractatus
entries.summary: A tractatus takes one season to write and has a limit on how many one author can write in a given Art or Ability.
quotes: It takes one season to write a tractatus.

entries.title: Copying Books
entries.summary: Careful copying keeps the original's quality; quick copying is three times as fast but lowers quality; the copyist's Profession: Scribe score drives the pace for summae.
quotes: COPYING CAREFULLY: 1 tractatus per season, or 6 + Profession (Scribe) points towards a summa.
COPYING QUICKLY: Three times as fast as careful copying, copy Source Quality is 1 lower than copied book.

entries.title: Standard Texts (Roots and Branches of the Arts)
entries.summary: Describes the widely available Roots of the Arts primers and the prized Branches of the Arts summae, which troupes may assign to Arts as needed for their saga.
quotes: These texts vary, but all have a Level of at least 7, and a Quality of at least 21.

alsoIn.title: Standard Texts (Roots and Branches of the Arts)

entries.title: Corrupted Copies
entries.summary: Lists the minimum language, Realm Lore and Magic Theory scores a scribe needs to copy a text without corrupting it, since a corrupted text is useless.
quotes: A corrupted text is useless.

entries.title: Hermetic Books: Definition of Categories of Value
entries.summary: Sidebar giving typical Quality ranges for summae and tractatus (excellent, sound, vain, discarded and legendary books) as a function of Level.
quotes: These Summae have a Quality of (25 – Level) or below.

entries.title: Acquiring Books
entries.summary: Overview of the Order's book trade: sale of finished books through Redcaps and Tribunals, and scribal hospitality in other covenants' libraries.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.101

entries.title: The Sale of Hermetic Books
entries.summary: Describes the four postal sale methods (public offer, tender, exchange, subscription) and how books are sold at Tribunal.

entries.title: Prices for Books and the Cow and Calf Oath
entries.summary: Introduces the Cow and Calf Oath, a Hibernian ruling restricting resale or gifting of purchased copies, which the later price guidelines assume has been sworn.

entries.title: Mundane Book Prices
entries.summary: Mundane books are bought with cash from a stationer, with a delay of a season for uncommon titles and a cheaper unbound paper version available.

entries.title: Hermetic Book Trade as Barter
entries.summary: Explains that Hermetic books are traded by barter and haggling, and that book values shift with events and with the vis a covenant holds.

entries.title: Least Expensive Books
entries.summary: Guidance on how damaged and discarded books are acquired, typically for about a pawn of vis per damaged summa, with cheap tractatus available in lots after a disaster.
quotes: A covenant wanting to purchase damaged summae with vis can usually find a seller for about a pawn of vis per book

entries.title: Vain Book Prices
entries.summary: Pricing guidance for vain summae and tractatus, and the warning that a vanity book bought from someone other than its author costs as much as a sound one.
quotes: Characters can usually purchase vain summae for half their level in pawns of vis

entries.title: Sound Book Prices
entries.summary: Guideline price in vis for ordering sound summae and tractatus from covenants with permanent copyists, including a surcharge for an immediately available copy.
quotes: These charge a number of pawns of vis equal to the book's level, if the purchaser is willing to wait a season for the copy to be produced.

entries.title: Excellent Books
entries.summary: Books of the highest Quality are normally gifts rather than purchases, with copying restricted; describes how Houses Bonisagus and Tremere handle them.

entries.title: Grammar: vocabularies and dictionaries as tractatus
entries.summary: Describes how grammar is taught and gives the one game rule in the section: vocabularies and dictionaries count as tractatus for the Latin Ability.
quotes: In game terms, dictionaries are equivalent to tractatus, the relevant Ability being Latin.

entries.title: Encyclopedias
entries.summary: Rules for treating encyclopedias as series of tractatus and for using them as a library for quick research: an hour's search, an Intelligence + Ability roll against an Ease Factor set by obscurity, with a bonus per relevant tractatus. Lists example encyclopedias.
quotes: treat every 5 books (or fraction) as a single tractatus on a given subject
each tractatus in an encyclopedia on the appropriate subject gives a +1 bonus to the Ability roll for that subject

entries.title: Translations
entries.summary: Sets the language and Artes Liberales requirements to translate texts, the time needed for a tractatus or summa, and the Quality penalties for language and cultural differences.
quotes: It takes a season to translate a tractatus.
Translated texts have their Quality reduced by 2, one for language differences and one for cultural differences.

entries.title: Lecture Commentaries
entries.summary: A teaching character can have a scribe record his lectures into a tractatus whose Quality derives from the teacher's Communication and the scribe's skill, optionally improved by editing. Commentaries do not count against the character's normal tractatus limit.
quotes: Lecture Commentary Quality: Teacher's Communication + scribe's Profession: Scribe/2
Edited Lecture Commentary Quality: Original Quality + 1 + bonuses from Virtues
A character can produce a number of lecture commentaries equal to his relevant Academic Ability score.

entries.title: The Manufacture of Books
entries.summary: Describes how a covenant produces a book, from author or notary to scribe, illuminator and binder, and the staff needed; writing speed depends on the lower of the author's and notary's totals.
quotes: The speed of this writing, as described in ArM5, page 165, is based on the Communication + Language total of either the author or notary, whichever is lower.

entries.title: Extended Quality of Books (introduction)
entries.summary: Introduces an optional, more detailed system in which a book's quality comes from author, scribe, binder and resonant materials, and can be reduced by secondary functions or damage.
quotes: This section presents a more complicated system, which allows troupes to improve covenant libraries through play and construct great tools of learning.

entries.title: Resonances and Clarification of Books
entries.summary: Resonant materials can add quality points to a book (one for purchased materials, one for materials from stories), and a third point comes from clarifying the book by enchantment and leaving it in a Magical aura; includes the sidebars on resonant components and a summary of quality rules.
quotes: A book's quality can be increased by one point if the book incorporates resonant materials that the covenant purchases.
A third point of Quality can be gained by clarifying a book.
The book must then be left in a Magical aura for (12 / aura strength) years

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material Bonus Table

entries.title: Potentially Resonant Book Components
entries.summary: List of the parts of a book (inks, pages, boards, ribbons, ornamentation, registers and so on) that can incorporate resonant materials.
quotes: The cover boards

entries.title: Summary of Quality Rules
entries.summary: Side-by-side summary of the core and extended formulas for summa and tractatus quality, including maximum quality, the effect of skilled artisans and the bonus for resonant materials.
quotes: Author's Communication + 6 + bonuses due to Virtues + bonus for writing to level less than half of Art score.
Quality may not exceed 2 x (Communication + Virtue bonuses + 6).

entries.title: Extended Quality Rules (Summa and Tractatus)
entries.summary: Extended formulas for maximum summa and tractatus quality, adding bonuses for skilled scribe, binder and illuminator and for mystical resonance, with the skill threshold for artisans and the bonus for each kind of resonant material.
quotes: A professional is considered to be skilled if she has a Profession score of 6 or more.
Resonant materials add +1 to quality if they are purchased items, +2 if they are rare items only to be gained from stories.

related.text: ArM5 p.110 Shape and Material Bonus Table

entries.title: Secondary Functions of Books
entries.summary: Book variants that trade quality for another purpose (damaged, edition de luxe, epitome, ex libris, exemplar, flap-bound, holographical, huge and congregational codices, juvenilia, palimpsest, unbound), each with its own quality modifier or restriction.
quotes: An exemplar has a –3 modification to quality.
A flap book has a quality modifier of –1 and cannot have resonant materials incorporated as cover ornamentation.
For the purposes of enchantment, a book has a material level of 2 and a size multiplier of 4.
A literate person may make 15 levels of juvenile copy in a season.

entries.title: Opus Types
entries.summary: Introduces the opus types, the styles of book that expand on the core summae and tractatus.

entries.title: Scriptoria
entries.summary: How mundane and Hermetic scriptoria work, including covenant copyists who need Magic Theory and Realm Lore to produce incorrupt copies.

entries.title: Other Opus Types
entries.summary: Rules for commentaries, correspondences, florilegia, folios, glossed books, inspeximuses, pictorial works, pamphlets and primers, including their quality bonuses, study restrictions and how they are bought at covenant creation.
quotes: A magus gains an extra experience point in each season in which he is engaged in useful correspondence.
If these minima are met, the tractatus all gain a +1 bonus to quality.
adds 1 to the quality of a book. It is performed during a season of reading.
which increases the level of his book by one-third of the difference between his current Art score and the Art score he had when he wrote the summa

entries.title: Prices for Books
entries.summary: Guidance on what Hermetic and mundane books cost, mostly in pawns of vis, by quality tier (mundane, damaged, vain, sound, excellent), including the Cow and Calf Oath restricting resale or copying.
quotes: Many Hermetic books are sold under a condition called the Cow and Calf Oath.
Characters can usually purchase vain summae for half their level in pawns of vis
These charge a number of pawns of vis equal to the book's level, if the purchaser is willing to wait a season for the copy to be produced.
A surcharge of up to 20% is added if there is a spare copy available for the impatient.

entries.title: Scribal Magic and Replacing Crafts
entries.summary: Introduces magic for scribes and librarians and gives the rule that when Finesse and Rego replace a mundane craft, the target scores for quality of goods rise.
quotes: when using Finesse and the Art of Rego to replace skill at mundane crafts, the target scores representing levels of quality of goods increase by at least 3 points.

entries.title: Rules for a Large Library
entries.summary: A way to record a big library as a single Level and Quality per Art or Ability: the best summa gives the base score and extra summae and tractatus add experience points to Level and Quality only if they are close enough to the library's current score.
quotes: Each Art and Ability is represented as a single Level and Quality that represents the sum total of the knowledge that the library has on that subject.
A book does not contribute an experience point to Quality unless its Quality is within three points of the library Quality

entries.title: Studying from the Library
entries.summary: How a magus studies from a large library: while the Art score is below the library's Level the library gives its Quality with a bonus, afterwards it gives only Quality for a limited number of seasons, and several magi studying one subject split the books; includes a worked example.
quotes: A maga whose score in an Art is less than the library's Level in that Art gains the library's (Quality + 3) in experience points in the relevant Art.

groups.title: Training animals and creatures
groups.intro: Taming and training animals and creatures over seasons.

entries.title: Training Creatures (Overview)
entries.summary: Introduces taming of animals with a Cunning characteristic, by magi, magical characters or mundane handlers, followed by further training in tricks.

entries.title: Taming Animals
entries.summary: Taming is a seasonal activity accumulating points over consecutive seasons until they exceed the creature's Might; the tamer may split points among creatures of one species up to a limit set by Animal Handling.
quotes: REQUIRED POINTS TO TAME A CREATURE: Might of the Creature, Minimum 1

entries.title: Taming Mundane Beasts
entries.summary: Sidebar giving mundane beasts an effective Might for taming purposes and noting that taming is a social activity so The Gift penalties apply.
quotes: mundane beasts have an effective (Animal) Might of 1 + 2 x Confidence Score

entries.title: A Hermetic Tamer
entries.summary: A magus tames an animal as a laboratory activity using a Rego (Form) Lab Total, producing a Lab Text that can later be reused to tame another creature of the same species.
quotes: TAMING POINTS ACCUMULATED EACH SEASON: Re(Fo) Lab Total – Creature's Might

entries.title: Hermetic Bonuses to Taming Lab Total
entries.summary: List of bonuses added to a Hermetic taming Lab Total: Animal Handling, Animal Ken, Experimentation and similar Lab Texts.
quotes: Animal Handling Ability Score
Animal Ken Ability Score

entries.title: A Mundane Trainer
entries.summary: Taming points per season for a mundane handler, who can usually only tame beasts with a small Magic Might.
quotes: Int + Animal Handling + Animal Ken – Creature's Might

entries.title: Tricks, Stunts, and Tasks
entries.summary: Who may command a tamed animal, and that a tamed animal is not considered to be under a continuing mystical effect.

entries.title: Loyalty
entries.summary: A tamed creature gains a Loyal Personality Trait towards its tamer; Loyalty Tests and extra seasons of training can raise or transfer that loyalty.
quotes: LOYALTY TEST: Loyal Personality Trait + stress die vs Ease Factor

entries.title: Training Animal Abilities
entries.summary: A character with Animal Handling can train a tamed animal's existing Abilities with the standard training rules, and the troupe may allow new Abilities subject to a Loyalty test.
quotes: make a Loyalty test for the animal against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: Trained Groups of Animals
entries.summary: A handler may lead tamed animals in combat as a trained group, using Animal Handling in place of Leadership, with exceptions to the usual Combat Score matching.
quotes: The character's Animal Handling Ability score is used instead of his Leadership Ability score

entries.title: Commanding a Creature
entries.summary: Roll to command a tamed beast against an Ease Factor set by how unusual, frightening or dangerous the task is, with Loyalty tests required for the most extreme tasks.
quotes: COMMAND BEAST: Presence + Animal Handling (or Ride or Magic Lore) + stress die vs Ease Factor

entries.title: Animal Training and Commanding Beasts
entries.summary: A trainer spends seasons building training points against an animal's Might, and once the animal is trained the trainer rolls to have it obey commands of varying difficulty. The same rules serve riders training mounts, who may use Ride in place of Animal Handling.
quotes: This total is the character's Intelligence + Animal Handling – Creature's Might.
a mundane animal is considered to have a Might score of 1 + 2 x Confidence Score
Presence + Animal Handling + stress die vs. a variable Ease Factor

entries.title: Taming Creatures
entries.summary: A seasonal activity in which a character accumulates taming points from Intelligence + Animal Handling until a threshold based on the creature's Confidence is exceeded, plus rules for commanding tamed animals, building or transferring their Loyalty, and training their Abilities.
quotes: The taming is complete when the accumulated total of points exceeds a total equal to 1 + (2 x the creature's Confidence Score).
Each additional season of training increases the Loyal Personality Trait by +1, to a maximum of +3.
make a Loyalty test for the animal against an Ease Factor of 6

entries.title: A Magical Trainer
entries.summary: Taming points per season for a character with the Master of (Form) Creatures Virtue, using Might, Animal Handling and Animal Ken minus the creature's Might.
quotes: Trainer's Might + Trainer's Animal Handling + Trainer's Animal Ken – Creature's Might

entries.title: Animal Ken and Animals
entries.summary: A character with Animal Ken can reason with any animal using Animal Handling to get it to follow an instruction without taming it, and can give tamed animals more complex commands.

groups.title: Aging and living conditions
groups.intro: Aging rolls, crises, Decrepitude, and the living conditions that slow aging.

entries.title: Aging
entries.summary: Yearly aging roll against the Living Conditions and Longevity Ritual modifiers, the Aging table (apparent age, Aging Points, Decrepitude), and the Crisis procedure, table, medical attention and Creo Corpus remedies.
quotes: AGING TOTAL: Stress die (no botch) + age/10 (round up)
CRISIS TOTAL: Simple die + age/10 (round up) + Decrepitude Score
Characters begin aging in the Winter after they turn 35.

entries.title: Living Condition Modifiers for Disease and Trade
entries.summary: Additional modifiers to the Living Condition modifier on the Aging Roll for lepers, those in a leper colony and those working in bad-air trades or mines, with a worked example.
quotes: A Living Condition modifier is applied to the Aging Roll (ArM5, page 170).

entries.title: Improving Living Conditions with Magic
entries.summary: Indirect magical improvement of living conditions for aging rolls, by long-term enchantments on the environment, at the cost of Warping for whatever is under the enchantments.
quotes: For every 40 levels of spells or enchantments used to improve the target living conditions, residents gain a +1 living conditions modifier.
targets under two level 20 enchantments gain two Warping Points each year
Targets under a single level 40 enchantment gain five Warping Points per year

groups.title: Warping
groups.intro: Warping Points from magic and the supernatural, and what they do.

entries.title: Warping (Hermetic Dangers)
entries.summary: Points to the full Warping rules in Long Term Events and notes that magi gain a Warping Point for each zero on botch dice when they botch a spell.
quotes: Note that magi gain one Warping Point for every zero on the botch dice when they botch a spell.

entries.title: Warping
entries.summary: Defines the Warping Score, advanced with Warping Points like an Ability, and gives the table of Warping Points needed per score.
quotes: To increase the Warping Score by one point, a character needs five times the new score extra Warping Points.

entries.title: Gaining Warping Points
entries.summary: Lists the four separate sources of Warping Points, all of which stack.
quotes: Living in a strong (6 or higher) supernatural aura.

entries.title: Warping from Living in Strong Auras
entries.summary: Table of Warping Points gained per period by aura strength and how much time is spent in the aura; characters whose own powers come from that realm are exempt.
quotes: Auras of over five points have an effect on anyone living within them

entries.title: Warping from Powerful Supernatural Effects
entries.summary: A Warping Point is gained from being subjected to a powerful supernatural effect not created by or specifically designed for you; sixth magnitude and higher Hermetic spells count.
quotes: any Hermetic spell of sixth magnitude or higher counts

entries.title: Warping from Constant Supernatural Effects
entries.summary: Characters continuously under supernatural effects gain Warping Points over time regardless of effect strength; explains what counts as constant, exceptions such as Parma Magica, and a summary table of effect types.
quotes: A character who is constantly under the influence of one or more active supernatural effects gains one Warping Point per year for each effect.

entries.title: Warping from Supernatural Botches
entries.summary: Botching the roll to invoke a supernatural effect gives Warping Points equal to the number of zeros on the botch dice.
quotes: she gains one Warping Point for every zero on the botch dice.

entries.title: Effects of Warping
entries.summary: What a rising Warping Score does to a character: more prone to Twilight for magi, and for mundane characters a progression of Minor Flaws, a supernatural Minor Virtue and then Major Flaws.
quotes: At a Warping Score of 6, and every point thereafter, the character gains a Major Flaw appropriate to the main sources of the warping.

entries.title: Warping and Non-Humans
entries.summary: Mundane creatures and things can be warped, but the storyguide just describes effects; creatures with a Might score are immune to Warping.
quotes: Creatures with a Might score are absolutely immune to warping.

entries.title: Warping While Under Constant Magical Effects
entries.requires: Constant enchantments on people or places
entries.summary: Tables showing how many Warping Points and what Warping Score and effects accumulate over the years for targets under constant enchantments that improve living conditions.
quotes: The second table assumes a single level 40 enchantment producing five warping points per year.

entries.title: Appropriate Virtues and Flaws for Warped Buildings
entries.summary: Suggests the kinds of Virtues, Flaws, magical Qualities and Personal Powers a building may gain when it becomes warped.
quotes: a Personal Power (an effect of Personal Range OR constant duration of up to 25 levels)

groups.title: Schools and universities
groups.intro: Parish, cathedral and monastic schools, universities and the life of a scholar.

entries.title: New Virtues and Flaws (Universities)
entries.summary: Explains how the new university Social Status Virtues work: only one is normally held, it need not be rebalanced as a character advances, every student has benefit of clergy, and the stages from student to doctor each build on the previous Virtue.
quotes: it is not necessary to balance Social Status Virtues after character generation
Every university student receives the benefit of clergy

entries.title: The Limits of Education
entries.summary: Caps the starting score of Academic Abilities by the type of school attended, with major subjects at full limit and minor subjects at half (rounded up), and lists which subjects each institution teaches.
quotes: Attending any of these schools demands that the character have the Virtue: Educated.
Minor subjects are limited to half the regular score limit listed below, rounded up.

related.text: ArM5 p.31 Age limits on Abilities

entries.title: Parish Schools
entries.summary: Describes how a character is accepted into a parish school with a social roll against a rural or urban Ease Factor, what the school costs and teaches, and how long a student typically stays.
quotes: Presence + Bargain or Charm or Guile + stress die vs. 6 (rural parish) or 9 (urban parish)
A student character studies two seasons out of the year from the parish priest.

entries.title: Cathedral Schools
entries.summary: Covers entry to a cathedral school (a social roll reduced by Bad Reputation), the cost of attending, how a character's Presence and Academic Reputation determine the number of students a cathedral teacher attracts, and the seasonal duties of a teacher.
quotes: Presence + Bargain, Charm, Guile or Intrigue + stress die – highest Bad Reputation vs. 12
A teacher can teach a number of students equal to five times the character's Teaching Ability
It costs a character one Mythic Pound to attend a cathedral school for one year.

entries.title: Monastic Schools
entries.summary: Monastic schools mostly admit their own brothers, use the cathedral school entry formula at a lower Ease Factor, and are of interest to magi chiefly for their libraries, which the precentor controls.
quotes: use the formula for gaining entrance to a cathedral school, but lower the Ease Factor to 9

entries.title: Urban Schools
entries.summary: Municipal schools admit citizens and foreigners using the cathedral school entry formula at different Ease Factors, and a master may teach as many students as his Teaching allows.
quotes: lower the Ease Factor to 9 if the prospective student is a citizen of the school's town. If he is a foreigner, make the Ease Factor 12.
(the teacher's Teaching score times five)

entries.title: Private Instructors
entries.summary: Explains the role of private instructors, the most common teachers at a Hermetic covenant, and how a character working as one owes his employer a share of each year.
quotes: The character will need to work for his employer for two seasons out of every year.

related.text: ArM5 p.72 Teachers bought with Build Points

entries.title: Warring Faiths
entries.summary: A character can write books or debate against another faith by combining two Theology Abilities, and gains extra Academic Reputation experience from such a challenge.
quotes: the character must average the scores in the two Theology Abilities to determine the maximum level of the summa
he receives double the normal amount of Academic Reputation experience points

entries.title: Acquiring a Teaching Position
entries.summary: An optional die-roll mechanic for finding academic work: a character spends a season and rolls against an Ease Factor set by the position, modified by Virtues and Academic Reputations. Failure wastes the season and a botch risks a wound or Bad Reputation.
quotes: Presence + appropriate Ability + Good Academic Reputation + bonus for Virtues – Bad Academic Reputation + stress die vs. Variable Ease Factor
If the roll fails, the season is wasted.

entries.title: Student-Run University
entries.summary: Describes the southern, student-governed model of university and gives sample statutes that bind masters, such as lecture attendance, original instruction and hosting disputationes.
quotes: A master must host a disputatio at least once a term.
A master may not read directly from the text during his lecture, but must offer commentaries and arguments that gloss the text.

entries.title: University of Masters
entries.summary: Describes the northern, master-governed model of university and gives sample statutes that bind students, such as dress, curfew, language and matriculation.
quotes: A student must always speak Latin, at class and in his residence.
A student must be matriculated into his faculty and must swear his Oath of Matriculation.

entries.title: False Scholars
entries.summary: A character can pose as a student to gain a university education without paying, rolling each season to avoid being discovered; success gives full experience, failure half, and a botch brings legal trouble.
quotes: Communication + Guile + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 9
Penalties from The Gift apply to this roll.

entries.title: Student Life
entries.summary: Covers how a student attaches to a master, matriculates and attends lectures, the costs of university life, and how copying a lecture text takes twice the normal time. A student character spends the usual two seasons a year on study.
quotes: Tuition, food, and rent usually cost a student two Mythic Pounds a year.
Overall, it takes twice as long as normal
ordinary lectures count toward a license and extra-ordinary lectures do not

entries.title: Academic Learning and Experience Points
entries.summary: Allows experience from being taught an Academic Ability to be split between that Ability and Latin or Teaching, with a minimum share going to the Ability taught, and similar rules for Latin and Artes Liberales.
quotes: He must put at least half of the gained experience points in the Academic Ability taught
If a player puts experience points gained from Latin instruction into Artes Liberales, he must put at least half of them in Latin.

entries.title: Examinations
entries.summary: A student faces a single, difficult private examination per career stage and then a ceremonial public examination that cannot be failed, with the candidate paying for the ceremony.
quotes: University students take only one exam per stage of their academic careers.
He cannot fail his public examination

entries.title: Passing Examinations
entries.summary: An abstract way to resolve a private examination: after the required years of study and a minimum Good Academic Reputation, the candidate makes an Exam Total against an Ease Factor set by the license. Passing the public examination only depends on paying for it.
quotes: Communication + Artes Liberales + Good Academic Reputation - Bad Academic Reputation + Stress Die vs. 6
A baccalaureate candidate needs a Good Academic Reputation of at least 1, a magister in artibus candidate 2, and a doctoral candidate needs a minimum score of 3.

entries.title: The Life of a Master
entries.summary: Describes a master's duties and the difference between resident and visiting masters. A master character teaches for part of each year and earns Exposure experience for those seasons.
quotes: Master characters must teach two seasons of every year

entries.title: The Mechanics of a Pilgrimage Story
entries.summary: Defines minor and major pilgrimages and a Pilgrimage Target Level for each desired outcome (gaining or losing Virtues and Flaws, removing traits, penance, miracles), plus limits on which Virtues and Flaws a pilgrimage can change.
quotes: A minor pilgrimage is one that requires a Target Level of 18 and that occurs in a single season, requiring a story.
A major pilgrimage is one that requires a Target Level of 30 and that takes multiple seasons, and possibly multiple stories, to play out.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.60 Miracles

entries.title: Oppositional Elements
entries.summary: How the storyguide builds a pilgrimage story from Oppositional Elements with assigned values that each pilgrim must personally overcome, with a table of example elements by value.
quotes: Total of Oppositional Elements Values = Pilgrimage Target Level
The Oppositional Elements for the pilgrimage should have total value at least equal to the Target Level of the Pilgrimage.

entries.title: An Example of a Pilgrimage Story
entries.summary: A worked example of setting Target Levels, totalling Oppositional Elements and tracking which characters overcome them on a major pilgrimage.

entries.title: Pilgrimage & Devotion
entries.summary: Gives the Devotion Points a Devoted character earns for pilgrimage to a saint's shrine and for further relevant sites and relics seen along the way.
